claim: Cohen, Malloy and Nguyen (NBER w25084, September 2018, revised March 2019; Journal of Finance 2020): on 1995-2014 US 10-K/10-Q filings, a value-weighted portfolio long non-changers and short changers (year-over-year textual similarity) earns 34-58 bp per month (t up to 3.59) over the following year; changes in the Risk Factors section give 5-factor alphas over 188 bp per month (t=2.76); there is no announcement return and the drift accrues over 6-18 months.
quote: earns a statistically significant 34-58 basis points per month
limitations: Sample ends 2014 and the working paper circulated from 2010 (SSRN 1658471), so 2015-2026 is post-publication; the 188 bp figure is one section-specific specification, the broad value-weighted effect is 34-58 bp per month; snapshot is pdftotext of the NBER PDF.
independent_replication: No large-universe post-2014 replication found on 2026-10-02; an S&P 100 replication (github iqueipopg/lazy-prices, March 2009-September 2026) finds -0.9% a year, FF5+MOM alpha t=-0.5, with full-document cosine saturated at a median 0.996.
verification_method: quote matched in the saved snapshot (tags stripped, whitespace collapsed) by the 2026-10-02 01:07 lead round
impact_on_spec: Defines the signal, the sign (non-changers outperform), the sections to test (full, Risk Factors, MD&A), the slow holding horizon and the prior magnitude (about 4-7% a year long-short before decay).
